cite: The Guardian, 'Irish church and police covered up child sex abuse, says report', 26 November 2009; RTÉ News, 'Litany of abuse in Dublin Archdiocese', 26 November 2009

fixes.d: The Commission of Investigation into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin reported on 26 November 2009. It examined a representative sample of 46 priests out of 102 within its remit; 320 people complained of child sexual abuse between 1975 and 2004. It found former Archbishops McQuaid, Ryan, McNamara and Connell failed to report what they knew to the Gardaí, and said the archdiocese's move to take out insurance against abuse claims showed it knew abuse was a potential major cost. It also criticised the Gardaí for treating priests as outside their remit; the Garda Commissioner called the report 'difficult and disturbing reading'.

note: Guardian confirms 46/102 sample, 320 complainants 1975-2004, four archbishops, Garda criticism. RTÉ confirms insurance finding. The 1987 insurance date and an explicit Garda Commissioner apology were not stated in the sources opened, so removed from d.

cite: Catholic News Agency, 'Former French priest convicted of sexual abuse of minors', March 2020; DW, 'France's top court clears Cardinal Barbarin in abuse case', 14 April 2021; Crux/AP, 6 March 2020; Vatican News, 4 July 2019

fixes.d: Fr Bernard Preynat was accused of abusing about 80 Boy Scouts between 1971 and 1991; many cases were time-barred and he was tried for assaults on 10 minors from 1986 to 1991. A church tribunal found him guilty and removed him from the priesthood (announced 4 July 2019), and on 16 March 2020 a Lyon court sentenced him to five years in prison. Cardinal Philippe Barbarin was convicted in March 2019 of not reporting him and given a six-month suspended sentence; an appeal court acquitted him in January 2020 and the Cour de cassation upheld that in April 2021. Pope Francis accepted his resignation on 6 March 2020.

note: Sentence, years, 80 victims, Barbarin conviction/acquittal/cassation and resignation all confirmed. Vatican News dates the defrocking announcement 4 July 2019 (not 5 July); added the 10 tried counts from CNA.
